speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a chronic wound on your right lower leg; can you tell me how long it has been present and what activities usually cause it to worsen?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-thrombotic syndrome with chronic venous insufficiency and stasis dermatitis.

Based on your history of DVT, 10-year swelling, and family history, the wound is likely due to poor venous circulation. To confirm this and check for infection or arterial issues, I need to see a venous duplex ultrasound and an ankle-brachial index (ABI). REQUEST TEST: Venous Duplex Ultrasound, Ankle-Brachial Index. REQUEST IMAGES: Right lower extremity wound and leg.
